title: A slot verb run where CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is unset is told its session does not exist, and a refused release leaves the lane held silently
body:
**A SLOT VERB RUN WHERE `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` IS UNSET IS TOLD ITS SESSION DOES NOT EXIST, AND A REFUSED RELEASE LEAVES THE LANE HELD WITH NOTHING SAYING SO.**

**What was seen.** vc's judge wrappers run in the background of vc's Claude Code session: `slots wait`, then `slots start`, the run, then `slots release`. On 2026-11-10 at about 21:15Z and on 2026-11-11 at 07:47Z the release was refused with `error: no Claude Code session file names session <id>` (`SlotError::NoSession`), although `slots start` from the same script had been accepted minutes earlier, and a foreground `slots release` from the same session seconds later was accepted both times. The request had a start and no end, so the lane read as running: on 2026-11-10 cargo sat held for 16 minutes until the desk asked.

**The cause, measured by cc on 2026-11-11.** Both refusing wrappers (`leg-0667.zsh` and `run-0707w.zsh`) ran `slots start`, then `unset ... CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR ...` for the test run, then `slots release` in the same shell. With the variable unset, `userstate::claude_dir()` falls back to `$HOME/.claude`, which does not exist on this host. `estate::read_sessions` answers a missing directory as an empty list, and `slots::caller` reports that as `NoSession`, whose remedy ("run it from inside a Claude Code session") is wrong for a caller that is inside one. Every wrapper that released without unsetting the variable released cleanly. The same class as issue 0671, a daemon started without the variable.

**What was ruled out.** A session file read while Claude Code rewrites it: 7,416,603 reads of a live session file over 150 seconds across 10 rewrites found no empty or unparsable read, and the file's inode never changed; a 10-minute watch over all 20 session files on the host saw 19 rewrites, no bad read and no file missing. So no retry is built.

**The fix (vc's ruling, size S).** (1) `slots::caller` and `slots::session_live` tell four cases apart, each with its own remedy: the sessions directory absent, naming the path read and whether `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` chose it; the directory unlistable; the session's own file unreadable, with its path and why; and no file naming the session. (2) The desk shows a start with no end whose asker's session is alive. A release accepted from the session id that `start.json` recorded is not built: it would paper over an environment in which every other slot verb still refuses.

**Found by** vc and devbin-vc during the 3.3.0 build; hv's standing rule puts it in 3.3.0.
